chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ghiyas ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat from the top of the tharid, and eat from its sides, for the blessing is in its top.'

key_terms.الثَّرِيد: Tharid, a traditional dish consisting of bread soaked in meat broth or sauce.
key_terms.الْبَرَكَة: Blessing, divine grace or abundance in sustenance.
key_terms.جَوَانِب: Sides or edges, referring to the outer parts of the dish.
key_terms.رَأْس: Head or top, referring to the uppermost layer of the food.

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for eating tharid according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates from Amir al-Mu'minin Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) regarding the etiquette of eating tharid, advising against consuming the top layer first to preserve the blessing (barakah) inherent in it. This practice reflects the broader Shia emphasis on mindful consumption and the spiritual significance of preserving divine favor in daily sustenance, linking physical nourishment to spiritual awareness.
